steps.say: A fair test finds out how one thing affects another. You change only one variable at a time.
The variable you change is the one in your question. The variable you measure is your result.
Every other variable must stay the same. These are the control variables.
steps.show: change 1, measure 1, keep the rest the same

steps.say: Before you start, write a prediction. Say what you think will happen and why.
Repeat each measurement and work out the mean. Repeating helps you spot results that do not fit.
Choose the right equipment, such as a thermometer, a forcemeter or a stopwatch.

check.prompt: Dina tests whether the size of a parachute changes how long it takes to fall. What should she measure?

options.why: That is the variable she changes.

options.text: the time it takes to fall

options.why: Colour is not part of her question, so she keeps it the same.
The drop height should stay the same.

hints: The variable you measure is your result.
Read her question again and find what she wants to know about.
Cross out the variable she changes and the ones she keeps the same.
check.explanation: Dina changes the size of the parachute and measures the time it takes to fall. Everything else stays the same.

check.prompt: Ravi times a ball rolling down a ramp three times: 2.4 s, 2.8 s and 2.9 s. What is the mean time?
hints: The mean is a kind of average.
Add the three times, then divide by 3.
check.explanation: 2.4 + 2.8 + 2.9 = 8.1, and 8.1 ÷ 3 = 2.7. The mean time is 2.7 seconds.
